candidate.answerReason: The unpainted cubes form an 8 × 8 × 8 interior cube. Subtracting its 512 cubes from the original 1000 leaves 488 painted cubes.

methods.label: Subtract the unpainted interior
methods.explanation:
It is easier to count the cubes with no paint. These are precisely the cubes inside the large cube, away from all six outer faces.

Along each of the three directions, exclude the first and last layers. That leaves \(10-2=8\) positions in each direction, so the unpainted interior contains
\[
8\cdot8\cdot8=512
\]
unit cubes. Every original cube is either unpainted or has at least one painted face. Thus the requested number is
\[
1000-512=\boxed{488},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\). Subtracting the interior counts each remaining cube once, including those at edges and corners.
methods.levelReason: The method requires only visualizing the interior cube, multiplying three edge counts, and subtracting from the total.

candidate.annotationRationale: Products of three edge counts determine unit-cube counts, matching the cube-volume node. Parts-and-total supports subtracting the disjoint unpainted interior. Cube structure and the meaning of unit volume are local prerequisites.

review.mathematicalCheck: A cube is unpainted exactly when its position avoids both outer layers in every direction. There are 8³=512 such cubes, leaving 1000−512=488; edge and corner cubes are each counted once.
review.levelCheck: The interior-layer reasoning and subtraction are clearly explained with elementary spatial reasoning and arithmetic.
